headings: Loan Production, Underwriting Standards and Credit Review
paragraphs: Hancock Whitney Corporation (the "Company") is registered with the Federal Reserve as a bank holding company and has elected to be treated as a financial holding company under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended. The Company provides comprehensive financial services through its bank subsidiary, Hancock Whitney Bank (the "Bank"), a Mississippi state bank, and other nonbank affiliates. Our principal executive offices are located at 2510 14th Street, Gulfport, Mississippi, 39501, and our telephone number is (800) 522-6542. Our common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "HWC."
At December 31, 2025, our balance sheet totaled $35.5 billion, with loans of $24.0 billion and deposits of $29.3 billion.

The Bank offers a broad range of traditional and online banking services to commercial, small business and retail customers, providing a variety of transaction and savings deposit products, treasury management services, secured and unsecured loan products (including revolving credit facilities), letters of credit and similar financial guarantees. The Bank provides trust and investment management services to retirement plans, corporations and individuals and provides its customers with access to investment advisory and brokerage products.

We offer other services through bank and nonbank subsidiaries. The Bank's subsidiaries Hancock Whitney Equipment Finance, LLC and Hancock Whitney Equipment Finance and Leasing, LLC provide commercial finance products to middle market and corporate clients, including leases and related structures. We have other subsidiaries of the Bank for purposes such as facilitating investments in new market tax credit activities and holding certain foreclosed assets. Our holding company's nonbank subsidiary, Hancock Whitney Investment Services, Inc., provides customers with access to fixed annuity and life insurance products, investment advisory services and also participates in select underwriting transactions, primarily for banking clients.

We operate primarily in southern and central Mississippi; southern and central Alabama; northwest, central and southern Louisiana; the northern, central and panhandle regions of Florida; certain areas of east and northeast Texas; and the metropolitan areas of Nashville, Tennessee and Atlanta, Georgia. At December 31, 2025, we had 180 banking locations and 221 ATMs across our footprint. Our operating strategy is to provide customers with the financial sophistication and range of products of a regional bank, while successfully retaining the commercial appeal and level of service of a community bank.

Our priority is to continue to grow revenue in our existing markets with controlled expenses while providing five-star service through enhanced technology and processes that make banking simpler for our clients. We have and will continue to invest in promoting new and enhanced products and services that contribute to the goal of diversifying our sources of revenue from both new and existing clients. We continue to make progress in our multiyear organic growth plan announced in late 2024 that includes both the hiring of additional revenue-generating associates and expanding our footprint in Florida and Texas. To-date, we have added a net 22 new bankers associated with this growth plan and expect to hire as many as 50 new bankers in 2026 that will support both commercial and business banking growth initiatives. We opened one new financial center in 2025 and expect to open four additional centers in 2026, all located in the North Dallas, Texas area. The May 2025 acquisition of Florida-based Sabal Trust Company expanded our trust and asset management business with the addition of their leadership team and clients, including approximately $3 billion in assets under management. This acquisition provides the opportunity to develop relationships and offer other private banking, wholesale and retail banking products and services in high-growth markets in the central Florida region. We also continue to evaluate future acquisition opportunities that have the potential to increase shareholder value, provided overall economic conditions and our capital levels would support such a transaction.
Additional information regarding the Company and the Bank is available at investors.hancockwhitney.com.

The Bank's primary lending focus is to provide commercial, consumer and real estate loans to consumers, small and middle market businesses, and corporate clients in the markets served by the Bank. In addition, and to a lesser degree, the Bank makes loans both regionally and nationally, generally through its specialty lines of business, including the equipment finance, commercial real estate and healthcare segments, often with sponsors in our market areas. We seek to provide quality loan products that are attractive to borrowers and profitable to the Bank. We look to build enduring, profitable client relationships over time and maintain a strong presence and position of influence in the communities we serve. Through our relationship-based approach, we have developed a deep knowledge of our customers and the markets in which they operate. We continually work to provide a consistent lending process across our banking footprint, to strengthen the underwriting criteria we employ to evaluate new loans and loan renewals, and to diversify our loan portfolio in terms of type, industry and geographical concentration. We believe that these measures position the
Bank to meet the credit needs of businesses and consumers in the markets we serve while pursuing a balanced strategy of loan profitability, growth and credit quality.

The following describes the underwriting procedures of the lending function and presents our principal categories of loans. The results of our lending activities and the relative risk of the loan portfolio are discussed in Item 7. "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations."

The Bank has a set of loan policies, underwriting standards and key underwriting functions designed to achieve a consistent lending and credit review approach. Our underwriting standards address the following criteria:
• guarantor requirements (including policies on financial statements, tax returns, and guarantees);
• appraisal requirements (and their review); • loan approval hierarchy;

• standard consumer and small business credit scoring underwriting criteria (including credit score thresholds, maximum maturity and amortization, loan-to-value limits, global debt service coverage, and debt to income limits);

headings: Risks Related to Economic and Market Conditions
Current uncertain economic conditions pose challenges, and could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
We may be vulnerable to certain sectors of the economy and to economic conditions both generally and locally across the specific markets in which we operate.
We are subject to lending concentration risk.

Certain changes in interest rates, loan origination, inflation, or the financial markets could affect our results of operations, demand for our products and our ability to deliver products efficiently.
Changes in the policies of monetary authorities and other government action could adversely affect our profitability.
The financial soundness and stability of other financial institutions could adversely affect us.
Tax law and regulatory changes could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
Governmental responses to market disruptions and other events may be inadequate and may have unintended consequences.
We may need to rely on the financial markets to provide additional capital.
Our investments in certain tax-advantaged projects may not generate returns as anticipated or at all and may have an adverse impact on our results of operations.
Risks Related to the Financial Services Industry
We must maintain adequate sources of funding and liquidity.
Greater loan losses than expected may adversely affect our earnings.
We depend on the accuracy and completeness of information about clients and counterparties.
We are subject to a variety of risks in connection with the sale of any loans.
We rely on other companies to provide key components of our business infrastructure.
The continued development and use of artificial intelligence (AI) presents risks and challenges that may adversely impact our business.

We, or third parties from whom we license critical information technology systems, have in the past been, and in the future may be alleged to have infringed upon intellectual property rights owned by others.
Employee misconduct could expose us to significant legal liability and reputational harm.
Our business may be adversely affected by fraud.
The value of our goodwill and other intangible assets may decline in the future.
Risks Related to Our Business Strategy
We are subject to industry competition which may have an impact upon our success.
The implementation of new lines of business or new products and services may subject us to additional risk.
paragraphs: We face a number of material risks and uncertainties in connection with our operations. Our business, results of operations and financial condition could be materially adversely affected by the factors described below.

While we describe each risk separately, some of these risks are interrelated and certain risks could trigger the applicability of other risks described below. Also, the risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones that we may face. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us, or that we currently do not consider significant, could also potentially impair, and have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, and financial condition.

We are operating in an uncertain economic environment. Our business and operations, which primarily consist of lending money to customers in the form of loans, borrowing money from customers in the form of deposits and investing in securities, are sensitive to general business and economic conditions in the U.S. Continued economic uncertainty and a recessionary or stagnant economy could result in financial stress on our borrowers, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations. Deteriorating conditions in the regional economies we serve, or in certain sectors of those economies, could drive losses beyond that which is provided for in our allowance for credit losses. We could also face the following risks with the following events:

• market developments (both domestic and international), the value of the U.S. Dollar in relation to the currencies of other advanced and emerging market countries, inflation and economic stagnation or slowdown may affect consumer confidence levels and may cause adverse changes in payment patterns, resulting in increased delinquencies and default rates on loans and other credit facilities;

• the processes we use to estimate the allowance for credit losses and other reserves may prove to be unreliable. Such estimates rely upon complex modeling inputs and judgments, including forecasts of economic conditions, which may be impaired during periods of heightened volatility or incomplete economic data reporting, and could therefore be rendered inaccurate and/or no longer subject to accurate forecasting;
• our ability to assess the creditworthiness of our borrowers may be impaired if the models and approaches we use to select, manage, and underwrite loans become less predictive of future charge-offs;

paragraphs: Net income for the year ended December 31, 2025 was $486.1 million, or $5.67 per diluted common share, compared to $460.8 million, or $5.28 per diluted common share in 2024. Included in the results of the year ended December 31, 2025 is a charge of $5.9 million (pre-tax), or $0.05 per share after tax, attributable to costs associated with the acquisition of Sabal. Included in the results of the year ended December 31, 2024 is a charge of $3.8 million, or $0.03 per diluted share after-tax, supplemental disclosure item attributable to a revision of the FDIC special assessment. The following is an overview of financial results for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to December 31, 2024:
• Net income of $486.1 million, or $5.67 per diluted common share, up from $460.8 million, or $5.28 per diluted share
• Adjusted pre-provision net revenue, a non-GAAP measure, totaled $679.9 million, up $38.8 million
• Provision for credit losses of $51.2 million in 2025, compared to $52.2 million in 2024; allowance for credit losses to total loans remains strong at 1.43% at December 31, 2025, down 4 basis points
• Loans of $24.0 billion, up $659.0 million, or 3% • Deposits of $29.3 billion, down $213.1 million, or 1%

• Tangible common equity ratio of 10.06%, up 59 bps; common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 13.65%, down 49 bps, reflecting the return of capital through our share repurchase program and an increase in shareholder dividends

• Credit metrics remain relatively stable, with criticized commercial loans down $87.7 million, or 14%, and nonaccrual loans up $9.5 million, or 10%; the net charge-off ratio was 0.22% compared to 0.19%
• Net interest margin expanded 10 bps to 3.47% • Efficiency ratio (a non-GAAP measure) improved to 54.78%, compared to 55.36%

The year ended December 31, 2025 was an outstanding year for our company. Net interest margin expanded ten basis points, adjusted pre-provision net revenue and return on assets grew, efficiency ratio improved, and credit quality remained stable. We deployed capital through the repurchase of 4.3 million shares of our common stock, increasing our quarterly shareholder dividends, and funding both organic and inorganic growth, including the acquisition of Sabal Trust Company on May 2, 2025. The Sabal acquisition expanded our trust and asset management business in Central Florida and provides opportunities to build relationships in that region. We experienced loan growth of 3% across our footprint and in most business segments, driven by increased demand and progress on our multi-year growth plan. We remain committed to continuing to fulfill our organic growth initiatives while maintaining operational efficiency and proactively managing capital to enhance shareholder value.

headings: 貸款發放、承貸標準與信用審查
paragraphs: Hancock Whitney Corporation (the "Company") 已經在聯邦儲備銀行登記為銀行控股公司，並選擇以根據1956年銀行控股公司法案（Bank Holding Company Act of 1956）修正後的規定，被視為金融控股公司。本公司透過其銀行子公司 Hancock Whitney Bank (the "Bank"), 一間密西西比州銀行，以及其他非銀行附屬公司，提供全面的金融服務。我們的總部位於密西西比州蓋爾波特市14街2510號，郵遞區號為39501，電話號碼為(800) 522-6542。我們的普通股在納斯達克全球選選市場交易，代碼為"HWC"。
截至2025年12月31日，我們的資產負債表總額為355億美元，其中貸款為240億美元，存款為293億美元。
銀行提供廣泛的傳統及網上銀行服務給企業、中小企業及零售客戶，提供多樣化的交易及儲蓄存款產品、財務管理服務、擔保及無擔保貸款產品（包括循環信貸設施）、信用證及類似財務擔保。銀行為退休計畫、公司及個人提供信託及投資管理服務，並為客戶提供投資顧問及證券經紀產品的存取權。

我們透過銀行及非銀行子公司提供其他服務。銀行的子公司 Hancock Whitney Equipment Finance, LLC 及 Hancock Whitney Equipment Finance and Leasing, LLC 提供商業金融產品給中型市場及企業客戶，包括租賃及相關結構。我們有其他銀行子公司用於促進對新市場稅收抵免活動的投資及持有某些被贖回的資產。我們的控股公司非銀行子公司 Hancock Whitney Investment Services, Inc. 為客戶提供固定年金及人壽保險產品、投資顧問服務，並參與部分發行交易，主要為銀行客戶。

我們主要營運於美國南部及中部密西西比州；南部及中部亞拉巴馬州；西北、中部及南部路易斯安那州；佛羅裏達州北部、中部及panhandle地區；東部及東北部德克薩斯州的部分地區；以及田納西州納什維爾市及佐治亞州亞特蘭大市的都會區。截至2025年12月31日，我們在營運範圍內擁有180個銀行營業點及221個ATM機器。我們的營運策略是為客戶提供區域銀行的金融專業程度及產品範圍，同時成功保留社區銀行的商業吸引力及服務水準。
有關本公司與銀行的額外資訊，請至 investors.hancockwhitney.com 查閱。

銀行的主要貸款重點是為消費者、中小企業及企業客戶在銀行服務的市場中提供商業、消費及不動產貸款。此外，銀行也較少程度地在區域及全國範圍內提供貸款，通常透過其專門業務線，包括設備融資、商業不動產及醫療保健部門，通常與我們市場區域的發起人合作。我們致力於提供對借款人有吸引力且對銀行有利潤的貸款產品。我們希望透過時間建立持久且有利潤的客戶關係，並在服務的社區中保持強大的存在與影響力。透過我們的關係導向方法，我們已對客戶及他們所處的市場有深入的瞭解。我們持續努力在銀行營運範圍內提供一致的貸款流程，以強化我們評估新貸款及貸款續約所使用的授信標準，並在貸款組合的類型、產業及地理集中度方面進行多元化。我們相信這些措施使我們處於有利位置
Bank 將滿足其服務市場中企業與消費者的信貸需求，同時追求貸款獲利性、成長與信貸品質的平衡策略。
以下說明貸款業務的授信程序，並介紹我們主要的貸款類別。我們的貸款業務結果及貸款組合相對風險，於第 7 項 "管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析" 中進行討論。
Bank 有一套貸款政策、授信標準及關鍵授信功能，旨在實現一致的貸款與信貸審查方法。我們的授信標準涵蓋以下準則：
• 保證人要求（包括財務報表、稅務申報及擔保政策）；
• 評估要求（及其審查）；• 貸款核准層級；
• 標準消費者及小型企業信貸評分授信準則（包括信貸分數門檻、最大到期日及償還期、貸款價值上限、全球債務償還覆蓋率及債務收入比率上限）；

paragraphs: 2025 年 12 月 31 日會計年度的淨收入為 486.1 百萬美元，或每股稀釋普通股 5.67 美元，與 2024 年 12 月 31 日會計年度的 460.8 百萬美元，或每股稀釋普通股 5.28 美元相比。2025 年 12 月 31 日會計年度的結果包含因取得 Sabal 而產生的費用 5.9 百萬美元（稅前），或稅後每股 0.05 美元。2024 年 12 月 31 日會計年度的結果包含因修正 FDIC 特別評估而產生的費用 3.8 百萬美元，或稅後每股稀釋普通股 0.03 美元，為補充揭露項目。以下為 2025 年 12 月 31 日會計年度與 2024 年 12 月 31 日會計年度的財務結果概覽：
• 淨收入為4.861億美元，或每股稀釋普通股5.67美元，較2024年12月31日財年4.608億美元，或每股稀釋普通股5.28美元為高
• 調整後的預備提列淨收入為非 GAAP 指標，總計為 679.9 百萬美元，較前一年增加 38.8 百萬美元
• 2025年信貸損失撥備為5,120萬美元，較2024年5,220萬美元為低；信貸損失撥備與總貸款比率維持強勁，於2025年12月31日為1.43%，較前一年下降4個基點
• 貸款為 24.0 十億美元，較前一年增加 659.0 百萬美元，或增加 3% • 存款為 29.3 十億美元，較前一年減少 213.1 百萬美元，或減少 1%
• 可用普通股權益比率為10.06%，較前一年增加59個基點；普通股一級資本比率為13.65%，較前一年減少49個基點，反映本公司透過股票回購計畫回饋資本及股東紅利增加
• 信用指標維持相對穩定，與前一年相比，被評為需關注的商業貸款減少 87.7 百萬美元，或減少 14%，且非應計貸款增加 9.5 百萬美元，或增加 10%；淨撥備比率為 0.22%，與 0.19% 相比
• 網路利息邊際擴張10個基點至3.47% • 效率比率（非GAAP指標）改善至54.78%，較前一年55.36%為低

本會計年度截至2025年12月31日為本公司表現卓越的一年。淨利息邊際擴張10個基點，調整後撥備前淨營收與資產回報率成長，效率比率改善，且信用品質維持穩定。本公司透過回購430萬股普通股進行資本配置，提高每季股東紅利，並資助內生與外生成長，包括於2025年5月2日收購Sabal Trust Company。Sabal收購擴大了本公司在中部佛羅裏達州的信託與資產管理業務，並提供在該地區建立關係的機會。本公司在全體營運範圍內各業務部門均實現3%的貸款成長，此成長由需求增加及多年度成長計畫的進展所驅動。本公司仍致力於持續履行內生成長計畫，同時維持營運效率，並積極管理資本以提升股東價值。

headings: 與經濟及市場狀況相關的風險
目前不確定的經濟狀況可能帶來挑戰，並可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
我們可能對經濟中某些產業部門及總體經濟狀況，以及我們營運特定市場的區域經濟狀況較為敏感。
我們面臨貸款集中風險。
利率變動、貸款發放、通貨膨脹或金融市場的變化，可能影響我們的營運成果、產品需求及產品交付效率。
貨幣當局政策的變更及其他政府措施，可能對我們的獲利能力產生不利影響。
其他金融機構的財務健全性與穩定性，可能對我們產生不利影響。
稅法及監管制度的變更，可能對我們的財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
政府對市場動盪及其他事件的回應可能不足，且可能產生未預期的後果。
我們可能需要依賴財務市場提供額外的資金。
我們對某些稅務優惠專案的投資可能無法產生預期的回報，甚至完全無回報，且可能對我們的營運結果產生不利影響。
與金融服務業相關的風險
我們必須維持充足的資金來源及流動性。
實際發生的貸款損失高於預期，可能對我們的獲利產生不利影響。
我們依賴對客戶及交易對手資訊的準確性與完整性。
我們在銷售任何貸款時，都會面臨多種風險。
與我們營運相關的風險
我們依賴其他公司提供我們業務基礎建設的關鍵零組件。
人工智慧（AI）的持續發展與應用，可能帶來風險與挑戰，並可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們，或從我們取得關鍵資訊科技系統授權的第三方，在過往曾被指控，或未來可能被指控，侵權他人所擁有的智慧財產權。
員工不當行為可能使我們面臨重大法律責任與聲譽損害。
我們的業務可能因詐欺行為而受到不利影響。
我們的商譽及其他無形資產的價值，未來可能下降。
與我們商業策略相關的風險
本公司受產業競爭影響，可能對本公司之成功產生影響。
新業務線或新產品與服務之實施，可能使本公司面臨額外風險。
paragraphs: 我們面臨許多重大風險與不確定性，與我們的營運有關。我們的業務、營運結果與財務狀況可能因下列所述因素而受到重大不利影響。
雖然我們分別說明每個風險，但其中一些風險是相互關聯的，某些風險可能觸發其他風險適用性。此外，下列所述的風險與不確定性並非我們可能面臨的唯一風險。目前我們尚未知悉，或目前認為不具重大影響的其他風險與不確定性，也可能對我們的業務、營運結果與財務狀況造成重大不利影響。

我們處於一個不確定的經濟環境中。我們的業務與營運，主要為以貸款形式向客戶提供資金、以存款形式向客戶借入資金，並投資證券，對美國的總體經濟與商業條件較為敏感。持續的經濟不確定性與經濟衰退或停滯，可能對借款人的財務狀況造成壓力，進而對我們的業務、財務狀況與營運結果產生不利影響。我們服務的區域經濟或這些經濟中的某些產業條件惡化，可能導致損失超過我們信用損失撥備所預估的範圍。我們也可能面臨以下風險與相關事件：
• 市場動態（包括國內與國際），美國美元與其他先進與新興市場國家貨幣的兌換率、通貨膨脹與經濟停滯或減速，可能影響消費者信心，並導致付款模式產生不利變化，進而導致貸款及其他信貸設施的違約率與違約率上升；
• 我們用來估計信用損失撥備及其他撥備的程序，可能被證明不可靠。這些估計依賴複雜的模型輸入與判斷，包括對經濟條件的預測，而在經濟波動加劇或經濟數據報告不完整期間，這些預測可能變得不準確，或不再能進行準確預測；
• 若我們用來選擇、管理與核准貸款的模型與方法變得無法預測未來的貸款違約率，則我們評估借款人的信用worthiness能力可能受到影響；
